get.description: Read a page of objects of the specified type. You can control the data returned by specifying the properties you want to include in the response. This endpoint is useful for retrieving a list of CRM objects with optional filtering and pagination capabilities.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: The paging cursor token of the last successfully read resource will be returned as the `paging.next.after` JSON property of a paged response containing more results.

parameters.name: archived
parameters.description: Whether to return only results that have been archived.

parameters.name: associations
parameters.description: A comma separated list of object types to retrieve associated IDs for. If any of the specified associations do not exist, they will be ignored.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of results to display per page.

parameters.name: properties
parameters.description: A comma separated list of the properties to be returned in the response. If any of the specified properties are not present on the requested object(s), they will be ignored.

parameters.name: propertiesWithHistory
parameters.description: A comma separated list of the properties to be returned along with their history of previous values. If any of the specified properties are not present on the requested object(s), they will be ignored. Usage of this parameter will reduce the maximum number of objects that can be read by a single request.

post.description: Create a CRM object with the specified properties and receive a copy of the object, including its ID. This endpoint is useful for adding new objects to your CRM system with predefined properties. Documentation and examples for creating standard objects are provided.

Location.description: URL of the newly created resource

post.description: Archive a batch of CRM objects identified by their IDs. This operation moves the specified objects to the recycling bin, effectively archiving them in bulk. It is useful for managing large sets of data that need to be archived simultaneously.

Create a batch of CRM objects in your HubSpot account. This endpoint allows you to create multiple objects at once by specifying their properties. The response will include a copy of each created object, including their IDs. This is useful for efficiently adding large sets of data to your CRM.

Retrieve a batch of CRM objects by their internal IDs or unique property values. This endpoint is useful for fetching multiple objects in a single request, allowing for efficient data retrieval. You can specify whether to include archived objects in the response.

parameters.name: archived
parameters.description: Whether to return only results that have been archived.

post.description: Update a batch of CRM objects in your HubSpot account. This endpoint allows you to modify multiple objects at once by providing their properties. It is useful for bulk updates where you need to change information across several records simultaneously.

Create or update a batch of CRM objects by unique property values. This operation allows you to either insert new objects or update existing ones based on the provided unique identifiers. It is useful for bulk operations where you need to ensure that objects are up-to-date or added if they do not exist.

Permanently delete a contact and all associated content to comply with GDPR regulations. This endpoint allows you to specify the contact using the 'idProperty' set to 'email' to identify the contact by their email address. If the email address is not found, it will be added to a blocklist, preventing its future use.

Merge two CRM objects of the same type in your HubSpot account. This operation combines the properties and associations of the specified objects, resulting in a single unified object. It is useful for consolidating duplicate records or integrating data from different sources.

Search CRM objects of a specified type using various filters and criteria. This endpoint allows you to query CRM objects by specifying filter groups, sorting options, and properties to include in the response. It is useful for retrieving a customized list of objects based on specific search parameters.

get.description: Read an object identified by `{objectId}`. By default, `{objectId}` refers to the internal object ID, but it can also refer to any unique property value specified by the `idProperty` query parameter. You can control the response content using the `properties` query parameter to specify which properties to return.

delete.description: Move an Object identified by `{objectId}` to the recycling bin. This operation is useful for temporarily removing objects without permanently deleting them, allowing for potential recovery or review before final deletion.

patch.description: Perform a partial update of an Object identified by `{objectId}`. `{objectId}` refers to the internal object ID by default, or optionally any unique property value as specified by the `idProperty` query param. Provided property values will be overwritten. Read-only and non-existent properties will be ignored. Properties values can be cleared by passing an empty string.
